zotero.abstractNote: This document presents a study on mitigating data contamination in the evaluation of large language models (LLMs) by employing a reasoning-driven synthesis approach. The authors synthesized 1,643 multi-step reasoning questions from 20,277 arXiv papers, demonstrating that their method effectively resists contamination and maintains performance stability across various model families. They advocate for a shift towards reasoning-driven benchmarks that prioritize genuine problem-solving abilities over memorization, and provide open-source resources for reproducibility.
